angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 848,754 km at 114.26 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7523 +/- 0.0141 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 114.26 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.22 +/- 0.06 solar radii from Hellier et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract): 848,754 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.19 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Hellier et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6050 +/- 50 K from Hellier et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hellier et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-166.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.341, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): spectral type F9 V, from Hellier et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.19 dex, from Hellier et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.2826, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): age 2.1 Gyr, from Hellier et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): rotation period 12.1 d, from Hellier et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 12.1 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-166 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 5.1 km/s, from Hellier et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.488.3067H/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.22 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 1.000. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
